# RBI raises repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50 amid challenging global environment
- IANS
- October 7, 2026 10:08 AM
New Delhi, Oct 7 (IANS) The Reserve Bank of India’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting -- led by Governor Sanjay Malhotra -- on Wednesday announced to raise key policy rate by 25 basis-points (bps), taking it to 5.50 amid a challenging global environment.
SDF rate stands adjusted at 5.25 per cent, and the marginal standing facility range and the bank rate to 5.75 per cent, said the RBI.
...
The Central Bank had kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25 per cent for quite some time.
The rate hike comes amid challenging factors, including rising inflation and crude oil prices above $100 a barrel driven by the West Asia crisis.
...
Economists had expected an increase in the repo rate for the first time since February 2023.

# RBI MPC hikes repo rate by 25 bps to 5.5% in Oct policy, changes stance to calibrated tightening
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra also announced that the standing deposit facility (SDF) rate under the liquidity adjustment facility (LAF) stands adjusted to 5.25 per cent, while the marginal standing facility (MSF) rate and the Bank Rate have been revised to 5.75 per cent.
The MPC also decided to shifts stance to calibrated tightening.
- Shrishti Sharma
...
- Updated On Oct 7, 2026 at 10:48 AM IST
The Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) on Wednesday decided to increase the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 per cent, citing rising inflationary pressures and risks of inflation becoming more broad-based.
The committee, which met on October 5, 6 and 7, voted unanimously in favour of the rate decision.
...
The MPC also decided to shifts stance to calibrated tightening.
Importantly, Governor said that the rate cuts are off the table in the near term, with future policy action likely to be either a rate hike or a pause, depending on evolving growth and inflation dynamics.
The MPC, however, voted 4-2 to change its stance to calibrated tightening.
